title: Agents for auto analysis and trades
author: Shuratt
selftext:
I’m trying to understand whether it’s realistically possible to build with Claude a set of AI agents that monitor a specific asset, apply a defined trading strategy on live data, and autonomously execute orders through a broker API.

Not looking for ready‑made products or courses.

I just want feedback from people who’ve actually tried this path to understand if it's doable in practice and worth investing time and research on it.

Thabk you for any feedback

comments.author: shadowalpha_ai
comments.body: Absolutely. I use the MCP from my platform (I can send you a link if you want to see more of an example) to pipe sentiment data for example from stock analysts on X and youtube into a central engine, which can then push trades with agentic help to the robinhood MCP. You can use Alpaca too.

comments.author: joshman1204
comments.body:
My agents use massive amounts of data that is invested from polygon/massive. I inject large amounts of context into the prompt and then give the agents a set is mcp tools to gather more of it wants.

Once it decides to trade the agent submits the trade to a validator that runs deterministic checks in rust and gives the agent a receipt if the trade passes. 

Once the agent is finished the report they're findings along with the trade receipt and rust handles the actual trade with ibkr/alpaca depending on the asset.

replies.author: Shuratt
replies.body: Noob question. Why the need of a validator?

replies.author: joshman1204
replies.body: Llms are bad at math and will generally hallucinate a close enough answer. The validation is just a way to allow the llm to focus on reasoning about the trade and not doing basic math.

comments.author: MycoHost01
comments.body:
Get your own data so you can feed the llm and prioritize a harness. I’m doing perp trading with DeepSeek being orchestrated by me and Claude or whatever top model I have access too. 

Is not a plug and play system start with a live sim trade if you can get data which is why is important you log everything the agent does all losses trades entries etc so you can study what it does and tune the harness.

comments.author: AttitudeGrouchy33
comments.body:
Doable, yes. Worth doing depends on where you put the autonomy.

I would not start with “Claude monitors an asset and places orders.” I’d split the system:

- deterministic strategy/risk layer
- broker/session health outside the model
- agent for research, thesis writing, and exception handling
- hard limits that the agent cannot negotiate with
- full diary before each action
- tiny size / paper mode until the boring failures are gone

The danger is that a good explanation starts feeling like a good trade. Those are different things.

The version I trust more is: the agent has a narrow job, visible mandate, visible trade diary, and fire criteria. If it breaks its own playbook, it loses authority.

comments.author: token----
comments.body: Our firm relies on a customized framework that uses timeseries forecasters along with rich context fed LLMs. This works well as we solely rely on MCPs with local models. The only problem is that running backtests or monte carlos are too much difficult with swarms of agents so you can only forward test the system
